content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposes an identifiability theorem to provide a guarantee to supervised controllable generation.
It's theorem ensures that semantic attributes can be disentangled and independently controlled by orthogonalization in latent space in a supervised manner. 
Based on the theoretical analysis, authors propose a general method for controllable generation, which can be integrated with most latent-variable generative models, and plug it into a pre-trained NVAE.
Experiments show that their method is comparable with the state-of-the-art methods in attribute-conditional generation and image editing to the merits of NVAE, and has advantages in efficiency and consistency.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength\
*Enough research over controllable generative models and their limits.\
*Developing NVAE for controllable generation, and open a new path towards controllable generation.\
*Discussion is based on identifiability theorem.

Weaknesses\
*Insufficient research over latent analysis models\
*Novelty and contributions weak:\
　It looks like the introduction of independent component analysis, ICA to NVAE.\
　What are the differences and novelties?\
　Orthogonality is necessary for independence, but since the solution space has been extended, doesn't this increase the computational 　cost?\
*Runtime analysis:\
　How fast and how much improvement did the proposed optimization bring?

The approach is theoretical, but the idea itself is an introduction to ICA, so there is little novelty and improvement.

content.title: Our theory is a novel identifiabiltiy theorem, not an introduction of existing ICA theory, and they are essentially different.
content.comment:
Thanks for your time and comments. We are pleased that you acknowledged the theoretical soundness of our work. We hope that our response can address your questions

Q1: The idea is an introduction of ICA.

A1: No, this is not true. Our theory is essentially different to ICA. In ICA, the labels of attributes (ground truth) are agnostic, and hence ICA is essentially unsupervised. Compared with this, our paper proposed an identifiability theorem with given labeled attributes, and hence our theory is essentially supervised. More importantly, our theory does not require priors of the ground truth to be independent, while ICA does. Therefore, our theory is suitable for the case of non-independent attributes, while ICA is not.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors focused on the study of the supervised controllable generative models, and proposed an identifiability theorem to provide controllability guarantee. Specifically, theoretically the semantics can be disentangled and independently controlled by orthogonalization in the latent space. Experiments have been implemented to compare the proposed method with some SOTA controllable generative models, which showed that the proposed method can reduce the generation time.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

Compared with some existing works the paper provided theoretical guarantee for the controllability. In particular, in theory the semantics can be disentangled and independently controlled by orthogonalization in the latent space, which is desirable for practical implementation. 


################### 

Weaknesses:

The theorem is somewhat elegant, but there are a lot of issues and questions with the implementation. 

. Section 3.4: In NVAE, the latent variables are divided into L groups. Any guidelines for such division?

. Section 3.4: It's not clear why it is necessary to transform the latent variable w in NVAE (and also in other possible generative models as mentioned in Section 3.3) via the normalization flow to the new latent z. Can you skip the normalization flow part and apply the method directly on w?

Experiments:

. The benchmarks used are all based on GANs. As the proposed method is NVAE-based and also GANs may have limitation on reconstruction, it would make sense to include some autoencoder-based benchmarks for comparison, such as Esser et al (2020) mentioned in Related Works. 

. In the implementation, only 12 groups of latent variables  in NVAE are used. Intuitively, these applied 12 groups are with smaller sizes and a lot of information would be lost. If all 36 groups are used can you further improve the performance. If not, can you provide some explanation for that? 

. Table 1: In terms of the performance of FID and ACC, the proposed method is worse than the LACE benchmarks for all cases. The authors mentioned that these scores might be improved by using more powerful normalizing flows. This should be tried and checked.

. Fig. 4: The authors claimed that the manipulation of each attribute does not change other attributes. This is not true. Obviously, in the top row by manipulating smile the age of the person is also changed (ie., from a kid to a woman). Also, as the background of these images is simply white, it's hard to see the disentanglement with the background. 

. Fig. 5: The authors claimed that the manipulation of each attribute does not change other attributes. This is not true. (a) the first row + age=45, the glasses are also removed. (a) the second row + glasses = 1, the age is also changed (similar to + age = 40).

. In experiment, does the latent z also include a z_{res} block to reflect the noise and unrelated attributes?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity and Quality: The paper is well presented. 

Novelty: The authors provided theoretical guarantee for the controllability to ensure that the semantics can be disentangled and independently controlled by orthogonalization in the latent space. However, there are a lot of issues in the implementation. 

Reproducibility: The authors have provided details about the training parameters and network architectures in the appendix. These would help to reproduce the experimental results.
content.summary_of_the_review: The authors provided theoretical guarantee for the controllability. However, there is a large gap between the theory and implementation In particular, although theoretically changing one attribute cannot affect other attributes experiments show that this claim is not true. Further explanation of the implementation is needed. Also, the benchmarks should include the autoencoder-based besides the GAN-based as the proposed method is built on NVAE. See the comments in Weaknesses above for more details.

content.title: Some comments about NVAE in this paper are not true.
content.comment:
Thanks for your time and comments. We are pleased that you acknowledged the novelty and theoretical soundness of our work. We hope that our response can address your questions

Q1：Why the latent variables in NVAE are divided into L groups?

A1: This is the original setting of NAVE, which aims at constructing a hierarchical structure of latent variables.

Q2: Why it is necessary to transform the latent variable w in NVAE?

A2: No, this is not necessary. Our method can be integrated with NVAE directly and jointly trained. For saving time of training, we propose a plug-in version for pretrained latent-variable generative models. This has been introduced in our paper.

Q3: Why only 12 groups of latent variables in NVAE are used?

A3: Because 12 groups are sufficient to control most global attributes (as introduced in the appendix of this paper). In image editing, the other groups are inferred by both the top 12 groups and input x, and hence the information of these spare groups is not lost (as their information is stored in x). That is, when we manipulate the top 12 groups of an image, the information of the spare groups is unchanged, which is advantageous for image editing.

Q4: The qualitative results have some drawbacks.

A4: We merely show some edited images without cherry picks. We have further improved the qualitative performance of our method, which will be shown in the revision.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper focuses on supervised controllable generation. In particular, the latent variable is enforced to be disentangled according to each given attribute (continuous or discrete) via orthogonal mapping. Such disengagement will enable efficient controllable generation later. More importantly, the proposed method can be plugged into a pre-trained generative model with latent variables, instead of requiring training from the scratch. Overall, the paper is well-written and easy to follow. However, some words are too absolute and there are some important related works that are missing.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength：

(1) This paper is well-organized and easy to follow.

(2) The latent disentangle based on orthogonal is interesting and promising. 

Weaknesses:

(1) Disentanglement in the latent space for controllable generation is not a new idea. There are a lot of related works that are missing in the paper. See [1][2][3] for disentangled representation learning for the controllable generation. 

(2) Enforcing orthogonal prediction for the attribute using the latent representation is also studied in the previous research, see [4]. The method proposed in [4] studied the same problem. Some deep discussions and empirical comparisons with [4] are necessary for the reader to better evaluate the contribution of the paper. 

(3) Some comments about GAN are not correct, e.g., most of them generally have difficulty in image editing since they base on GANs. Specifically, it is expensive to obtain the latent code of a given image using GANs...  I totally disagree with this claim. First of all, the latent code is not necessary for controllable generation, especially image editing. Meanwhile, there are already many good works for this same task based on GAN, see [5]. 

(4) ..., other semantics like background are often inconsistent due to the GANs’ weak reconstruction ability.... Disagree. Actually, adding reconstruction loss into GAN model is a common practice to address this issue, see [5][6]. 

(5) The experiment evaluation is a bit weak. As suggested previously, some relevant baselines based on VAE or GAN should be added for a fair comparison. 

(6) The image for showcase in Figure 4  is simple. It is incorrect to draw a conclusion that "Each attribute is disentangled with other semantics, including background and other attributes." More complex images should be edited with explicit backgrounds and nonrelevant attributes. 

(7) The comparison in Figure 5 is unfair. At least all the methods should be compared using the same image. 

Reference:

[1] Du, Y., Guo, X., Wang, Y., Shehu, A. and Zhao, L., 2022. Small molecule generation via disentangled representation learning. Bioinformatics (Oxford, England).

[2] Du, Y., Guo, X., Cao, H., Ye, Y., & Zhao, L. (2022). Disentangled Spatiotemporal Graph Generative Models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2203.00411.

[3] Lample, G., Zeghidour, N., Usunier, N., Bordes, A., Denoyer, L., & Ranzato, M. A. (2017). Fader networks: Manipulating images by sliding attributes. Advances in neural information processing systems, 30.

[4] Li, X., Lin, C., Li, R., Wang, C., & Guerin, F. (2020, November). Latent space factorization and manipulation via matrix subspace projection. In International Conference on Machine Learning (pp. 5916-5926). PMLR.

[5] Wu, P. W., Lin, Y. J., Chang, C. H., Chang, E. Y., & Liao, S. W. (2019). Relgan: Multi-domain image-to-image translation via relative attributes. In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF international conference on computer vision (pp. 5914-5922).

[6] Yinghua Yao, Yuangang Pan, Ivor W. Tsang, Xin Yao. TRIP: Refining Image-to-Image Translation via Rival Preferences. arXiv preprint arXiv:2111.13411

content.title: This paper has identifiability guarantee, while most works for disentanglement do not.
content.comment:
Thanks for your time and comments, which is helpful for improving this paper. We are pleased that you acknowledged the novelty and theoretical soundness of our work. We hope that our response can address your questions

Q1: Disentanglement in latent space for controllable generation is not a new idea.

A1: Specifically, the starting point of this paper is not disentanglement in latent space, but the linearization and orthogonalization of latent space, which has identifiability guarantee. This setting brings some advantages like efficient controlling as introduced in this paper (but disentanglement cannot), which are not introduced in previous works.

Q2: Some related works are missing.

A2: Thanks for pointing out this. As our paper focuses on image generation and editing, some recommended papers are not very related, but this suggestion is helpful for us. 

Q3: Some claims about GANs are hasty.

A3: We agree that these claims need more discussion and evidence. We will deliberate them in revision.

Q4: Some experimental settings are not proper.

A4: We will improve these settings in the revision
